title: A Sign Against Egypt and Cush

questions.question: In the year that the commander in chief, who was sent by whom, came to Ashdod and fought against it and captured it?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:1 (ESV): "who was sent by Sargon the king of Assyria,"

questions.question: At that time the LORD spoke by whom?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:2 (ESV): "the LORD spoke by Isaiah the son of Amoz,"

questions.question: Go, and loose the sackcloth from your waist and take off your what from your feet?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:2 (ESV): "and take off your sandals from your feet,"

questions.question: And he did so, walking naked and what?
As my servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot for how many years?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:3 (ESV): "for three years as a sign and a portent"

questions.question: So shall the king of Assyria lead away the Egyptian captives and the Cushite exiles, naked and barefoot, with buttocks what?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:4 (ESV): "with buttocks uncovered, the shame of Egypt."

questions.question: Then they shall be dismayed and ashamed because of Cush their hope and of Egypt their what?
And the inhabitants of this coastland will say in that day, "Behold, this is what has happened to those in whom we what?"
To whom did they flee for help to be delivered from the king of Assyria?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:6 (ESV): "and to whom we fled for help to be delivered from the king of Assyria!"

questions.question: Is Sargon mentioned in this chapter the same as Sennacherib?
The sign of Isaiah walking naked and barefoot was a portent against which two nations?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:3 (ESV): "a sign and a portent against Egypt and Cush."

questions.question: Ashdod was a principal city of the whom?
The Tartan (commander in chief) is a title used in which empire?
The inhabitants of this coastland refers to the people of where?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 20:6 (Context of Ashdod and the coast).

key_verse_text: And the LORD said, "As my servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot for three years as a sign and a portent against Egypt and Cush, ..."
